status.label: In the normal range
status.explanation: Your HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over roughly the last 2–3 months and is below the 5.7% threshold used for prediabetes.

summary: Your HbA1c of 5.4 is in the normal range, which is a great sign for your long-term health. Your BMI of 17.6 falls into the underweight category, so it's worth paying attention to steady, balanced nutrition to support a healthy body weight. Keeping up with regular check-ins on HbA1c and blood pressure, staying lightly active, and working toward your calorie target of 1700 per day are good next steps to protect your wellbeing going forward.

foods_to_eat: Whole grains like brown rice, millets and whole wheat
Pulses and legumes such as moong dal, chana and rajma
Paneer, curd and milk for protein and calories
Nuts and seeds like almonds, walnuts and peanuts
Healthy fats like ghee and nut butters in moderate amounts
foods_to_avoid: Deep fried snacks like samosas and pakoras on a regular basis
Refined flour items like maida biscuits and white bread
Excess tea or coffee instead of meals
Skipping meals, which can make it harder to meet your calorie needs
plan.portion_guidance: Since your BMI is in the underweight range, focus on eating regular meals and snacks without big gaps, and include an extra spoon of ghee, nuts or nut butter where you can to help meet your calorie target of 1700 kcal without feeling too full at once.
plan.hydration: Drink around 8 to 10 glasses of water through the day. You can also include a glass of milk or a fruit smoothie to add gentle calories along with fluids.
based_on: underweight BMI: calorie dense, frequent meals

exercise: Start with light, enjoyable activities like yoga, gentle bodyweight exercises, or a dance class 2 to 3 times a week, since you are currently lightly active.
Gradually build toward about 150 minutes a week of moderate activity, such as brisk walking, cycling, or swimming, adding a little more time each week.
Include muscle-strengthening exercises on 2 days a week, such as bodyweight squats, push-ups, or light resistance band work, to help build healthy muscle mass.
Focus on activities that support strength and stamina rather than calorie burning, since your goal is to maintain healthy weight, not lose it.
lifestyle.walking_goal: Begin with a 15 to 20 minute walk, 4 days a week, and build up gradually to 30 minutes a day, 5 to 6 days a week, at a comfortable pace.
lifestyle.weight_management: Your BMI falls in the underweight category, so the focus should be on nourishing your body well and supporting healthy muscle and strength gains rather than losing weight. Eating regular, balanced meals with enough protein, healthy fats, and whole grains can help you reach a healthier weight over time. A registered dietitian can help you build a meal plan suited to your vegetarian, Indian food preferences.
lifestyle.sleep: Aim for 7 to 9 hours of sleep each night. Try to keep a consistent bedtime and wake time, avoid screens for at least 30 minutes before bed, and keep your room cool, dark, and quiet to support restful sleep.
stress: Practice deep breathing exercises, such as inhaling for 4 counts and exhaling for 6 counts, for a few minutes when you feel stressed.
Try mindfulness or meditation apps for 5 to 10 minutes a day to help calm your mind.
Consider gentle yoga or stretching, which can help reduce stress while also supporting your physical activity goals.
behaviour_change: Keep a simple journal of your meals and activity to notice patterns and celebrate small wins.
Since you don't smoke or drink, keep up these healthy habits as they support your overall wellbeing.
Set small, achievable weekly goals, like adding one more day of walking, to build confidence and consistency.

monitoring.name: HbA1c
monitoring.why: Regular screening finds changes before symptoms appear.
monitoring.frequency: Every 3 years, or yearly if your doctor advises because of risk factors

monitoring.name: Blood pressure
monitoring.why: High blood pressure multiplies the heart and kidney risks of high blood glucose.
monitoring.frequency: At every doctor visit; at home regularly if you have high blood pressure

preventive_actions: Aim to consistently meet your daily calorie target of 1700 to support healthy weight gain
Include a variety of protein-rich vegetarian foods, like lentils, dairy, and legumes, at each meal
Keep up light daily activity such as walking or stretching, and gradually build in more movement as comfortable
Schedule regular blood pressure checks and routine HbA1c testing to continue tracking your health
Get enough sleep and manage stress, since both can affect appetite and metabolism

Is my current activity level appropriate, or should I consider increasing it gradually?

hba1c_caveat: HbA1c can be less accurate if you have anaemia, kidney disease, a recent blood transfusion or certain haemoglobin variants.
